title: The Number of Full Rounds You Have Played
statement:
An online chess tournament runs on a 24-hour clock and starts a new 15-minute round at every quarter hour: `00:00`, `00:15`, `00:30`, and so on up to `23:45`, every day.

You log in at `loginTime` and log out at `logoutTime`, both strings in the form `"hh:mm"`. When `logoutTime` is earlier than `loginTime`, your session runs through midnight and ends at `logoutTime` on the following day. The two times are never equal.

Return how many rounds you played in full: rounds that began at or after your login and finished at or before your logout.
constraints: loginTime and logoutTime have the format hh:mm
notes:
## Intuition

Rounds are fixed 15-minute slots, so counting them is arithmetic on minutes. Turn both times into minutes after midnight. A round fits only if it starts at or after the login, so the first usable slot boundary is the login rounded **up** to a multiple of 15; it must end by the logout, so the last usable boundary is the logout rounded **down**. The rounds in between are the answer. A brute force could test each of the 192 slots in two days one by one; the rounding does it in O(1).

## Approach

1. Convert `loginTime` to `start` and `logoutTime` to `end`, in minutes since midnight.
2. If `end < start`, the session crosses midnight: add 24 * 60 to `end`.
3. `firstRound = ceil(start / 15)` is the index of the first slot that begins after login.
4. `lastRound = floor(end / 15)` is the index of the boundary at or before logout.
5. Return `lastRound - firstRound`, but never less than 0.

## Example 1, step by step

`"09:31"` gives `start = 571` and `"10:14"` gives `end = 614`, no midnight wrap. `firstRound = ceil(571 / 15) = 39` (09:45) and `lastRound = floor(614 / 15) = 40` (10:00). One round, 09:45 to 10:00, fits: the answer is `40 - 39 = 1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(1): a fixed amount of parsing and arithmetic.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- A short session inside one slot, such as `"00:47"` to `"00:57"`, gives `lastRound - firstRound = -1`; clamp it to 0.
- Round the login up and the logout down; rounding both the same way overcounts.
- Only wrap when logout is strictly earlier; the times are never equal.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `start` | login time in minutes after midnight |
| `end` | logout time in minutes, plus a day if it wrapped |
| `firstRound` | index of the first quarter hour at or after `start` |
| `lastRound` | index of the last quarter hour at or before `end` |

narration.2: Turn the login time into minutes after midnight.
narration.3: Do the same for the logout time.
narration.4: A logout earlier than the login means the session crossed midnight...
narration.5: ...so the logout happens a full day (1440 minutes) later.
narration.7: The first round you can play fully starts at the login rounded up to a quarter hour.
narration.8: The last full round must end by the logout rounded down to a quarter hour.
narration.9: Count the slots between them; a session inside a single slot would give -1, so clamp at 0.
